lessons.title: Docker Image vs Container and Build Context
lessons.why: Understand what is captured at build time and what should arrive at runtime.
objectives: Explain Docker Image vs Container and Build Context using a concrete runtime/data-flow model.
Implement the smallest working example and predict its behavior before execution.
Diagnose a controlled failure related to Docker Image vs Container and Build Context using evidence rather than random edits.
Transfer the concept into the TaskFlow project without copying the finished example.
lessons.mentalModel: Package, verify, release, deploy, smoke-test, and roll back TaskFlow with explicit evidence at every stage.
beforeYouCode: Open a scratch file or the relevant TaskFlow package.
Run the existing project/tests once so you know the baseline is healthy.
State what evidence will prove success before changing code.
steps: Write the goal in observable terms before coding: by the end of this lesson you should be able to demonstrate “Docker Image vs Container and Build Context” in a running TaskFlow-oriented example.
Read the example once without running it. Predict the exact output, state change, request, or compiler behavior and write that prediction down.
Type the example yourself rather than pasting it. Run the narrowest command that exercises only this concept, then compare observed evidence with your prediction.
Change one assumption at a time. Keep the change small enough that you can explain why the result changed.
Perform the intentional failure lab: COPY . before install and observe how every source edit invalidates dependency-cache layers.
Read the resulting compiler error, stack trace, HTTP response, browser evidence, database state, or CI log from the first line that is actually relevant to your code.
Repair only the root cause. Re-run the same verification so you can prove the repair changed the observed evidence.
Close the reference and rebuild the important part from memory. If you cannot explain why each boundary exists, revisit the smallest missing concept rather than memorizing the final code.

example.code:
FROM node:24-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
COPY . .
example.expected: The image contains application/runtime dependencies; runtime secrets are not baked into it.

lessons.breakIt: COPY . before install and observe how every source edit invalidates dependency-cache layers.
debugChecklist: What did you predict?
What actually happened?
At what boundary do those first differ?
What is the smallest piece of evidence that proves the failure lives there?
Can you fix the cause without changing unrelated layers?
Can you add a regression test or repeatable verification?

exitTicket: I can explain why Docker Image vs Container and Build Context exists.

example.code:
name: CI
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: corepack enable
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm lint
      - run: pnpm typecheck
      - run: pnpm test
      - run: pnpm build
example.expected: A failing quality gate blocks a trustworthy merge when branch protection requires CI.

lessons.breakIt: Remove frozen-lockfile, modify package.json without committing the lockfile, and explain why CI becomes less deterministic.
